name: twoai-site

scripts.prebuild: node scripts/audit-check.mjs && node scripts/gen-icons.mjs && node scripts/fit-covers.mjs && node scripts/fetch-content.mjs
scripts.postbuild: pagefind --site dist && node scripts/url-guard.mjs && node scripts/canonical-noindex-sync.mjs && node scripts/sitemap-noindex-prune.mjs && node scripts/empty-render-check.mjs

comment_supply_chain: Build integrity: the Cloudflare build command is `npm ci` (NOT `npm install`), so every deploy installs the exact tree in package-lock.json rather than floating ^ ranges to whatever published since the last build. A poisoned patch release cannot enter a build without a lockfile change in a reviewed commit. The prebuild audit-check.mjs HARD-FAILS on a missing or drifted lockfile, and LOGS npm audit findings without failing: a hard audit gate would let an npm registry outage take deploys down, which trades a supply-chain risk for an availability risk. Keep the lockfile committed and let Dependabot open the version-bump PRs.
comment_astro: Astro was upgraded from 4.16 to 7 on 2026-09-21 (commit 76c448a), which cleared the critical advisory (GHSA-26w7-cxv4-gfx2) and the high ones in sharp, vite and esbuild. Before shipping it was built in WSL against the live content bundle: 15,032 pages, url-guard dropped 0, empty-render clean, and all three custom build hooks (unlistedManifest, capParagraphsInHtml, neutraliseDeadLinks) ran with the same counts as the Astro 4 build. The Cloudflare build then passed its own npm audit with no high or critical advisories. Upgrade Astro again the same way: build in WSL first, compare page count and the hook lines, then push.
